 Tools to help make sense of Medicare 
 By TO Acorn Staff 
 on 
 November 20, 2026 
 There are certain things in life that seem to get more complicated with age. Technology comes to mind. So do television remotes, airline reservations and trying to reach an actual human being when calling customer service.
 But Medicare may deserve a category all its own.
 Just when you think you understand your Medicare coverage, another open enrollment period arrives, complete with new premiums, changing drug formularies, provider networks and a mailbox full of brochures promising better benefits.
 And let’s not forget the television commercials featuring smiling seniors playing pickleball, walking on the beach and enthusiastically discussing their Medicare Advantage plans. I don’t know about you, but I’ve never seen anyone quite that excited about health insurance.
 Still, the decisions we make about Medicare matter. The wrong choice can mean discovering that your favorite doctor is no longer in your network, a prescription you’ve taken for years suddenly costs considerably more, or a procedure requires authorization you didn’t know you needed.
 This year, paying attention to those changes matters more than ever. Across the country, millions of Medicare beneficiaries are enrolled in plans that will be discontinued at the end of 2026. In Ventura County, several Medicare Advantage plans are also changing.
 For those affected, that could mean making important decisions about coverage for the coming year. Even if your plan isn’t changing, it’s worth taking another look. The plan that worked beautifully for you last year may not be the best choice for next year.
 Fortunately, there is help available, and here’s the best part: It’s free. It’s called HICAP, which stands for Health Insurance Counseling and Advocacy Program. Admittedly, not the catchiest name, but what it offers is pretty remarkable.
 HICAP provides free, confidential, unbiased Medicare counseling. Its trained counselors can help you understand the differences between Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage, compare prescription drug coverage, navigate supplemental insurance options and make sense of the alphabet soup of Parts A, B, C and D. 
 Unlike insurance agents, HICAP counselors don’t sell insurance or receive commissions. Their role is simply to help you understand your options so you can make an informed decision.
 Think of it as having a knowledgeable friend who understands Medicare and is willing to help you sort through the options, explain the terminology and answer your questions.
 HICAP can also help with Medicare billing questions, coverage denials, appeals and the sometimes-complicated relationship between Medicare and Medi-Cal.
 Another reason to seek reliable guidance is the growing number of Medicare-related scams. Open enrollment brings out not only insurance advertisements but also scammers, who are more than happy to offer unsolicited “help” in exchange for your Medicare number or personal information.
 A good rule of thumb: Don’t give your Medicare number to someone who calls unexpectedly, no matter how official they sound.
 Medicare’s annual open enrollment period runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7. That gives beneficiaries an opportunity to review and, if appropriate, change their coverage for the coming year. My advice? Give yourself plenty of time to sort through your options before the Dec. 7 deadline. And don’t assume that   doing so   is necessarily   the   best  choice. Gather your current insurance information, make a list of your medications, identify the doctors and hospitals you want to continue using, and ask questions.
 You don’t have to become a Medicare expert. You just need access to someone who is.
 In Ventura County, HICAP services are available through the Ventura County Area Agency on Aging. For more information or assistance, call 805-477-7300 or 800-434-0222, email HICAP@venturacounty. gov or visit vcaaa.venturacounty.gov/our-services/medicare-help/. 
 Medicare may never be simple, but having access to knowledgeable people who can help us understand our options makes the process a little less daunting.
 Now, if only someone could explain why I need three different remotes just to watch television.
 Andrea Gallagher is a certified senior advisor and president of Senior Concerns, a nonprofit agency serving Ventura and western Los Angeles counties. For more information, go to seniorconcerns.org or email agallagher@seniorconcerns.org .
